It is possible that means of communication other than direct access occurred between the sites, for example using smoke for visual signals, fire when it was dark or communication by sound using voices or beating stones which can be heard for several kilometres.

paragraphs.source_en: As is evident from the unequal qualities and quantities of paintings and their location in the landscape, the selected sites probably had different functions. Without a deeper analysis, Soleilhavoup (2007) noticed the existence of two categories of shelters; one with complex compositions which could have been a place for ceremonies, and the other with only a few figures which were probably expressions of individuals. He also mentions that some sites are intentionally hidden in the landscape and could have been designated for initiates, whilst others are exposed and well visible.

paragraphs.source_en: According to Sansoni (1994) walls with numerous paintings indicate that the place was frequented and new images added; superimpositions of various Round Head styles would testify that the place was visited over a long time span when styles changed. In my opinion, superimpositions of various Round Head styles may also signify that the site was used by various groups creating Round Heads of a different style, so that the styles are not necessarily chronological indicators.

paragraphs.source_en: The large compositions in many sites are likely to indicate that their creation was not the work of a single individual but of a number of people. The quantity of colours had to be considerable and often images are large (several metres high), or placed in a position impossible to reach without a support. The fact that many individuals invested energy in image-making may suggest that the place was not only known but also important. I suggest that large compositions were intended to be seen by more individuals; in the case of large scenes exposed in external parts of stone cities or in wadies it is likely that they were for public viewing. In the case of compositions hidden inside stone cities it is possible that they were designated to be seen by only a certain kind of person, for example by the initiates, who would have known the way to find them.
